# A native critical occupation that no normalizable fugacity makes cheap

29 October 2026. New all-occupation construction; root has independently whole-read and accepted the stated analytic scopes. No finite Fock-space fixture is used as a theorem. This attacks the critical-number interface left open by the normal-fluid and bounded-cut samplers. It is a scoped obstruction to grand-to-canonical filtering and fixed-slice critical-mode replacement, NOT a general sampling or fixed-density hardness result.

## 1. A fixed, stable, genuinely frustrated source

There are three sites and two bosonic flavors. In physical units choose

```
T = [ 3  1 -4
      1  3 -4
     -4 -4  8 ],
H = b†Tb+c†Tc+sum_(i=1)^3 (nb_i-nc_i)^2.
```

T has eigenvalues 0,2,12 and normalized zero vector `u=(1,1,1)/sqrt(3)`. For example it is `v1 v1^T+2 v2 v2^T`, v1=(1,-1,0), v2=(1,1,-2). The hopping triangle product is `1*(-4)*(-4)=16>0`, invariant under site phases. Three negative stoquastic hopping entries would have negative product. Thus this is a frustrated hopping input; all diagonal one-body terms are retained.

The Hamiltonian is positive, number conserving, and noncommuting. Define it by its finite particle-number blocks and their nonnegative direct sum. The potential is EXACTLY q_i^2, q_i=nb_i-nc_i. Expanding it into normal-ordered quartics includes its linear number term; that term is not discarded or hidden in the chemical potential. Couplings do not grow with occupation.

At fixed n_b,n_c, let N=n_b+n_c. Write b0,c0 for the u modes and define total depletion

`D=N-b0†b0-c0†c0 >=0`.

The spectral data give the operator inequalities

`2D <= H_hop <=12D`.                                  (1)

`J_b=i(b0†bv-bv†b0)`, `J_c=i(c0†cv-cv†c0)`, `J=J_b-J_c`.

# A critical-number interface fails even with perfect grand sampling

29 October 2026. Root has whole-read and accepted the all-occupation analytic theorem at its stated scopes. The independent review is [../../root_boson_ensemble/CRITICAL_MODE_REVIEW.md](../../root_boson_ensemble/CRITICAL_MODE_REVIEW.md).

The fixed native three-site Hamiltonian has PSD frustrated hopping with eigenvalues 0, 2, 12 and the physical noncommuting interaction `sum_i(nb_i-nc_i)^2`. All couplings and one-body diagonal terms are fixed; no occupation cutoff or attractive instability is added.

The main construction changes the critical-mode question in three ways:

* An exact mode-current uncertainty bound gives `H_N>=sqrt(N/12)-1` on EVERY particle sector. The exact zero-chemical-potential grand trace and all its finite number moments are therefore finite.
* An explicitly normalized, number-squeezed trial has sublinear energy `O(K^(2/3) log K)` at K particles per flavor. Hence every common fugacity r>1 makes the grand trace divergent. For EVERY normalizable fugacity, even with a perfect physical grand sampler, the probability of the desired K,K count is at most `binom(K+2,2)^2 exp[beta-beta sqrt(K/6)]`. Adaptive fugacity choices and positive mixtures retain this stretched-exponential postselection obstruction.
* Every FIXED imaginary-time slice count has a polynomial lower tail in K, while the exact trace has a stretched-exponential upper tail. At L=1 the balanced critical grand trace diverges, although the exact physical trace is finite. A declared log-partition error forces at least `Omega(sqrt(K)/log K)` slice growth. This is a necessary mesh condition, not a sufficient mesh theorem or a continuous-time runtime bound.

An exact product-zero-mode projection costs potential energy 4K/3, whereas the number-squeezed trial has sublinear energy and vanishing depleted fraction. Thus knowing the one-particle zero mode and a small depleted fraction does not qualify the interacting critical Gibbs weights.

# Whole review of the native critical occupation obstruction

29 October 2026. Root independently read critical_boson_mode/PROOF.md and
reconstructed its all-occupation arguments. The scoped interface obstructions
are accepted. No many-body diagonalization, stochastic run or independent
replay of its finite exact-data program is claimed by this review.

For the displayed frustrated three-site PSD kinetic matrix, its eigenvalues
0,2,12 and uniform zero mode give 2D<=H_hop<=12D. The summed one-particle
trace-distance estimate, relative-number/current commutator and Robertson
bound correctly yield H>=sqrt(N/12)-1 on EVERY sector. That coercivity
beats the polynomial sector dimensions and makes the exact r=1 grand
trace finite, including all finite number moments.

The squeezed trial is normalized with a paid multinomial-cell lower bound;
it is not an oracle for a useful squeezed state. Its discrete-gradient
depletion estimate and classical tilt entropy bound give the actual
o(K) variational energy. Thus every r>1 diverges on the balanced subsequence.
The normalizable fugacity domain and vacuum denominator then give a uniform
stretched-exponential upper bound on the high-K count probability. Mixing,
free-mode access, number readout and fugacity selection do not remove it.
Positive mixtures retain the same bound. Non-Gibbs umbrellas, importance
proposals and temperature changes are outside that postselection no-go.

Root also checked the finite-L positive-transfer Jensen argument. Its
multinomial collision lower bound is polynomial in K at every fixed L;
L=1 gives a harmonic divergent balanced grand trace despite exact physical
trace finiteness. The necessary Omega(sqrt(K)/log K) mesh growth follows
from the displayed log-partition inequality. No trace-uniform Trotter
limit or general continuous-time runtime lower bound is inferred.

Finally the product-zero-mode projection costs exactly 4K/3 potential
energy, whereas the squeezed trial is sublinear with vanishing depleted
fraction. Small depletion alone therefore does not qualify Gibbs weights.
The full ordinary fixed-mode canonical matrix has polynomial dimension in K
and is explicitly granted as an escape. This is high OCCUPATION on three
sites, not fixed-density bulk hardness or an ordered-matter solver. Poor
trial constants and historical novelty remain visible limitations.
